subject: Evidence packet for Business Continuity / RTO-RPO questions (Novus Bank)
messages:
From: Jordan Mitchell <jordan.mitchell@novusbank.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kerry O'Neill <kerry.oneill@ciso-consulting.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Request: RTO/RPO evidence and BCP runbook snapshot

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the overview call yesterday. As part of our SIG + procurement review, the risk team has asked for concrete evidence for your business continuity and disaster recovery commitments. Specifically we need: 

- A recent snapshot showing configured RTO and RPO values for customer-facing inference services (or explanation if values are operationalized differently).
- Excerpts from your incident runbook that describe failover steps for primary inference clusters and the expected timeline for recovery.
- Any SOC 2 control mappings or evidence that tie DR testing to control IDs (if available).

We need the package by end of next week to stay on schedule with the vendor review. Can your team provide PDFs or docs, and a short contact for technical follow-up?

Best,
Jordan
Lead, Third‑Party Risk
Novus Bank

--
External note: Kerry from CISO Consulting copied for coordination and to help triage requests.

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Mitchell <jordan.mitchell@novusbank.com>
Cc: Kerry O'Neill <kerry.oneill@ciso-consulting.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: RTO/RPO evidence and BCP runbook snapshot

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear list. Attaching an evidence packet that should address the items you called out. High level:

- redwood_rto_rpo_snapshot_20260512.pdf — automated snapshot exported from our monitoring system showing configured RTO/RPO targets per product tier (hosted API, dedicated, private).
- runbook-summary-2026-05-12.docx — redacted runbook excerpts describing detection, failover to alternate region, KV cache warmup, and customer notification timeline.
- soc2-control-matrix.csv — mapping between internal DR tests and SOC 2 CC controls we reference in our annual report.

Technical follow-up: Sergio Alvarez (CC'd) will be your technical lead for any deep DR/operational questions. Evelyn is looping to track procurement timelines.

A couple of notes you might see in the artifacts: our RTO policies differ by deployment mode — hosted API aims for sub-5m detection and automated traffic failover with RTO target of 30 minutes for critical workloads (higher tiers). Private deployments are customer-managed for infrastructure; we provide runbook and optional assisted DR for Dedicated customers under contract. We tried to keep the runbook excerpts redacted for customer data and internal IPs.

If you want a walkthrough I can ask Sergio to do a 30‑minute session next week (demo of failover and logs).

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0147

[attachments: redwood_rto_rpo_snapshot_20260512.pdf (pdf), runbook-summary-2026-05-12.docx (docx), soc2-control-matrix.csv (csv)]

Monica —

Appreciate the packet. Quick clarifications after a first pass (copying relevant excerpt):

> "hosted API aims for sub-5m detection and automated traffic failover with RTO target of 30 minutes for critical workloads (higher tiers)."

Can you confirm whether the 30-minute RTO is an operational SLA for paid customers (i.e., contractual) or an internal target? Also, we saw entries in the snapshot listing an RPO of "near-zero" for KV cache — can you add a short note in the runbook excerpt to explain how you persist/replicate KV cache state across regions and the expected window of any data rebuild?

Last question: do you have a recent DR test date and outcome summary we can reference (pass/fail + duration)? If you have a ticket or postmortem link that would be ideal.

Thanks — if easier, Sergio's technical walkthrough would be useful; we could take that instead of an extra doc update.

Best,
Jordan

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Mitchell <jordan.mitchell@novusbank.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Kerry O'Neill <kerry.oneill@ciso-consulting.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: RTO/RPO evidence and BCP runbook snapshot

Hi Jordan — Monica, thanks for the quick turnaround. I'm happy to take the walkthrough and provide the clarifications Jordan asked for. Quick answers inline: 

- RTO status: For Hosted API customers we publish operational RTO targets by tier; the 30‑minute RTO for critical workloads is an operational target that we include in SLA attachments for higher tiers (we can provide the contractual clause under NDA if needed). For standard hosted tiers the target is 2–4 hours depending on fallthrough escalation policies.

- KV cache: KV state is asynchronously replicated to a cold replica in a separate AZ/region with continuous snapshotting. On failover we accept a short rebuild window where warmup scripts restore most of the cache in ~8–12 minutes; the worst-case rebuild for cold entries is included in the RTO calculations and documented in the runbook excerpt (see section 3b). We will add a 2–3 sentence clarifying note to the runbook doc to make this explicit for reviewers.

- DR test: Our most recent full DR tabletop + partial live failover test was run 2026-03-10. Outcome: pass (minor automation bug fixed, documented in postmortem SEC-454). Duration from simulated outage to validated traffic in alternate region was 43 minutes (includes manual verification steps). I've attached the postmortem summary and linked the Jira for your reference.

Next steps: if you'd like the walkthrough, propose two 30‑minute slots next week and I'll schedule. Otherwise I'll update the runbook excerpt and resend a short addendum.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai

[attachments: postmortem-SEC-454-summary.pdf (pdf)]
